challenges.headline: Undefined notification recipients
challenges.premise: The request assumes 'the right people' is self-evident and can be resolved later without changing the design.
challenges.alternative: Route by Contact role (operational vs HR vs billing) plus the freelancer's internal manager, configurable per client, since the platform already models Contact roles for exactly this purpose.
challenges.consequence: Building with a hardcoded recipient (e.g. always the operational contact) means every client with a different routing need forces a rebuild, not a config change.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm the recipient list and whether it varies by client before writing the routing logic.

challenges.headline: Single fixed lead time
challenges.premise: The request implies one threshold for 'about to end' (e.g. a flat N days) applies everywhere.
challenges.alternative: Treat lead time as a configurable business rule scoped by client or contract type, consistent with how other thresholds already vary in this platform.
challenges.consequence: A hardcoded constant works for the first client and breaks the moment a second client wants a different lead time or multiple staggered reminders.
challenges.recommendation: Validate with the client whether lead time must be configurable now, or can safely stay global for v1.

challenges.headline: Notification treated as isolated
challenges.premise: The ask is scoped as a standalone 'send an alert' feature, separate from what happens after — renewal, final invoicing, validation.
challenges.alternative: Design the trigger as a generic 'end-of-mission approaching' event that notification is the first subscriber to, so final invoicing and validation can subscribe later without re-touching the trigger.
challenges.consequence: Building notification as a one-off means the next end-of-mission feature (e.g. auto-draft final invoice) requires rebuilding the same date-watching logic from scratch.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm with the client whether this is the first piece of a broader end-of-mission workflow before locking the architecture.

briefs.problem: Freelance missions can lapse unnoticed because there's no proactive signal before the end date, so renewal, extension, replacement sourcing or final invoicing get triggered too late.
briefs.solution: A configurable pre-end-of-mission alert tied to the Mission's end date, routed to the right stakeholder(s) through a defined channel, coordinated with the existing end-of-mission automation.

challenges.headline: Standalone alert vs renewal workflow
challenges.premise: The request treats this as a simple notification, independent of what happens next.
challenges.alternative: Since end-of-mission already triggers downstream automation (final invoicing, validation), design the pre-end alert as the entry point of a renewal/extension/replacement decision, not a disconnected message.
challenges.consequence: An isolated alert risks duplicating or conflicting with the existing end-of-mission automation, and stakeholders will still need a manual side-process to act on it.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm with the client whether this alert should open a decision workflow (renew/extend/replace) or stay a passive reminder before designing the trigger.

challenges.headline: Single fixed lead-time threshold
challenges.premise: The request implies one 'about to end' threshold that applies uniformly.
challenges.alternative: Make the lead time a per-client/contract configurable rule, or even staged (e.g. 30/15/5 days), since business rules on this platform routinely vary by client and contract.
challenges.consequence: Hardcoding a single threshold means the first client needing a different lead time, or multiple staged reminders, forces a rebuild of the trigger logic.
challenges.recommendation: Validate with account/ops teams whether the threshold needs to vary per client before locking the trigger design.

challenges.headline: Static schedule vs dynamic recompute
challenges.premise: The alert can implicitly be scheduled once from the mission's end date at creation time.
challenges.alternative: Since missions get extended or cancelled, recompute or invalidate the pending alert whenever the end date changes, rather than firing from a stale snapshot.
challenges.consequence: Without this, an extended mission still triggers a false alert on its original end date, undermining trust in the whole notification.
challenges.recommendation: Treat mission-date changes as a first-class trigger for alert rescheduling/cancellation, not a side edge case.

complexity_reasons: configurable threshold and routing rules per client
briefs.cost_driver: the configurable lead-time rule combined with role-based notification routing
risks: Overlap or conflict with the existing end-of-mission automation (final invoicing, validation) if the two triggers aren't explicitly coordinated.
Wrong or missing recipients if routing is hardcoded to 'the manager' instead of using the Client/Contact role model already in place.
Stale or duplicate alerts when a mission's end date changes after the alert is scheduled.
Permissions for who can configure thresholds or routing are undefined, risking client-specific settings leaking or being editable by the wrong role.

Extend this into a general renewal/offboarding decision workflow shared between missions and contracts.

challenges.headline: Notification framed as the whole feature

challenges.headline: Single hardcoded lead-time threshold
challenges.premise: The request implies one fixed 'about to end' definition works for all missions.
challenges.alternative: A per-client (or per-contract) configurable threshold avoids forcing a one-size-fits-all rule onto a platform where notification and business rules are already client-specific configuration.
challenges.consequence: A hardcoded threshold will need a follow-up change request the first time a second client needs a different lead time — a rebuild rather than a config change.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm with the client whether the lead time should be configurable now or can safely be fixed for a first release.

challenges.headline: 'The right people' left undefined
challenges.premise: The request assumes a single, self-evident set of recipients.
challenges.alternative: Routing by the Client Contact's role (billing, HR, operational) — the pattern already used elsewhere on the platform — lets the same event notify different people depending on what they're expected to do (a billing contact for final invoicing, an operational one for renewal).
challenges.consequence: Guessing a generic recipient (e.g. 'the client') risks notifying nobody who can actually act, or everyone regardless of relevance.
challenges.recommendation: Map notification recipients to Contact roles before build, not during testing.
